text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- CAIXA FEDERAL, TREASURY DISPUTE FCVS DEBT

A dispute between federal bank Caixa Economica and the National Treasury over who should claim 2.5 billion reais in old housing debt has slowed plans to securitize some 50 billion reais in mortgage debt in the FCVS fund.
-- CARDOSO TO MEET WITH HASHIMOTO TODAY
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso will meet with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto to discuss Brazil's controversial auto import regime.
The release of first-half earnings for Brazilian banks shows it is difficult to generalize about the overall performance of the sector.
-- ECONOMIST KILLED BY STRAY BULLET IN SAO PAULO
An economist was killed by a stray bullet that was fired through his 11th floor apartment in the upper middle-class Sao Paulo neighborhood of Brooklim.
-- CESAR MAIA IS TARGET OF MAYORAL CANDIDATES
Rio de Janeiro Mayor Cesar Maia's spending habits have become the chief target of candidates vying for the post in upcoming elections.
-- LOW SALARIES MAKE WOMEN ATTRACTIVE JOB CANDIDATES
Businesses prefer hiring women over men in Sao Paulo because they earn on average 33 percent less than men.
-- THREE SUSPECTS CONFESS TO KILLING WOMAN AT BAR
Three of five suspects in the highly publicized murder of a 23-year-old college student in a Sao Paulo bar have confessed to the crime.
